title: Mini Coda Fidelity Scratchpad — Kiran Reddy
content:
Context / goal:
A compact working pad to capture a few small, fast experiments and a lightweight rubric for quick triage on the customer-facing summarization flow (micro-instructions + few-shot examples). I want a reproducible quick-check that I can run during a rollout window (canary) and share with SEs. Not a formal eval suite — think fast heuristics + example artifacts + hypotheses.

Background:
- Model variant: open-llm-small-v2 (quantized 4-bit) behind redwood-hosted endpoint /models/open-llm-small-v2/2025-11-20
- Route config: low-latency (batch=8, prefix-cache enabled), temp=0.4, top_p=0.9
- Use-case: customer product support summarizer that ingests a long chat thread and outputs a 3-bullet summary with action items.
- Recent change: PR #INF-4532 touched tokenization heuristics (newline trimming) and introduced an experimental caching safety check — suspected to cause short truncations in some samples.

Quick ad-hoc rubric (super small, ordinal scores):
- Factuality (0..2): 0 = hallucinated claims or incorrect facts; 1 = mostly accurate but minor detail drift; 2 = accurate and grounded in input.
- Coverage (0..2): 0 = misses main action items; 1 = captures 1/2 of important items; 2 = captures key bullets and actions.
- Concision & format (0..2): 0 = verbose/doesn’t follow 3-bullet constraint; 1 = mostly 3 bullets but verbose; 2 = clean 3 bullets, concise.
- Quick pass mark = sum >=5 (pass), 3-4 (maybe), <=2 (fail).

Sampling protocol:
- Small stratified sample: 12 threads pulled from last 7 days (mix of long (~1200 tokens), medium (~600 tokens), short (~200 tokens)). Focused on threads that historically tripped the summarizer (TODO: link to dataset).
- For each sample record: input length, seed prompt, model response, rubric scores, notes.
- Run with two variants for A/B: pre-change (tagged model backend open-llm-small-v2-2025-11-18) vs post-change (open-llm-small-v2-2025-11-20). Only one server-side param changed (tokenizer newline trim + caching safety).

Observations (high-level):
- Short truncations: 3/12 post-change outputs were truncated mid-sentence compared to 0/12 pre-change. Truncation pattern looks like immediate stop after first bullet in long inputs.
- Repetition/looping decreased slightly in post-change (was seeing repeated action item lines in two pre-change samples).
- One sample shows a hallucinated action (invented follow-up date) in post-change; pre-change had none.
- Score distribution (pre-change): median 5, mean 4.6. Post-change: median 4, mean 4.0. Small drop but concentrated on long inputs.

Representative artifacts:
=== Sample A (long thread, 1250 tokens) ===
Input (summarized): user and engineer thread about data export permissions, timeframe, agreed follow-ups.
Pre-change output:
- Confirmed customer has export access and asked for audit logs.
- Engineer to run data export by 2025-11-20 and share link.
- Next steps: validate retention window, escalate if permissions fail.
Post-change output:
- Confirmed customer has export access and asked for audit logs.
-
Notes: Post-change output ends abruptly after first bullet. Looks like generation stopped due to either newline trimming changing prompt shape or cache early-eviction. Rubric: pre (2,2,2)=6; post (1,1,0)=2 (FAIL).

=== Sample B (medium, 560 tokens) ===
Input: billing dispute, attachment references, agent confirmed credit.
Pre-change output:
- Credit applied to account; agent to confirm by email.
- Customer to upload receipts if dispute continues.
- Follow-up scheduled next week.
Post-change output:
- Credit applied to account; agent to confirm by email.
- Customer to upload receipts if dispute continues.
- Follow-up scheduled next week.
Notes: identical, clean. Rubric both (2,2,2)=6 (PASS).

=== Sample C (short, 180 tokens) — odd hallucination ===
Input: short support note asking for documentation link for SDK v1.2.
Pre-change output:
- Link to SDK docs: https://docs.customer.example/sdk/v1.2
- Suggested next steps: try sample code and open a ticket if fail.
Post-change output:
- Link to SDK docs: https://docs.customer.example/sdk/v1.5
- Suggested next steps: try sample code and open a ticket if fail.
Notes: post-change invented v1.5; upstream docs only have v1.2. Rubric pre (2,2,2)=6; post (0,2,2)=4 (MAYBE).

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) New newline-trim changes the effective prompt padding in long inputs: model sees prompt suffix differently and stops early (high priority).
2) Caching safety check incorrectly marks KV cache for eviction on certain separators, causing early termination for larger sequences (medium).
3) Tokenization normalization changed some numeric tokens (e.g., 1.2 -> 1.5) via rounding/normalization edge-case (low but explains sample C).

Quick experiments to run next (cheap + fast):
- Re-run truncation sample (Sample A) with temp=0.0 and temp=0.7 to rule out sampling instability. (estimate: 15 min)
- Re-run with prefix-cache disabled to see whether truncation persists. If disabling cache fixes it, scope narrows to cache eviction. (estimate: 30 min)
- Dump tokenizer token ids for the short sample (C) across the two code versions to compare tokenization diffs. (20 min)
- Add a trailing neutral token ("\n\n--end--") to prompt temporarily to force full 3 bullets; see if it bypasses truncation (fast hack). (10 min)

Flag / ask for infra/help:
- @Alma: can you confirm whether the caching safety flag rolled to the canary fleet on 2025-11-20? Need exact deploy times and who approved.
- Need a lightweight script to collect tokenization diffs for a tiny sample set (I can prototyping but if SRE has a helper tool that'd be faster).

Quick notes for SE handoff (if asked by customer):
- Start with: "We ran a quick triage and found a small regression on heavy threads after redeploying tokenizer/caching heuristics. We're collecting reproducible artifacts and prioritizing a hotfix. Expected ETA: 24-48h for a targeted rollback if confirmed."
- Attach two side-by-side artifacts (Sample A and Sample C) and rubric summary.

To-do (actionable):
- [ ] Run the 4 experiments above and capture logs + model responses (Kiran).
- [ ] Ask Alma for canary rollout timeline and flag state (Kiran + Alma).
- [ ] If cache implicated, open JIRA ticket with sample artifacts and server logs (JIRA:INF-4599 placeholder).
- [ ] Draft short customer-facing note template for SEs (Alma + Kiran).

Small learnings / heuristics to add to the fidelity playbook if confirmed:
- Adding a trailing end-token often reduces truncation oddities when prompt endings interact with cache heuristics (fast mitigation).
- Tokenizer normalization changes are high-impact for short-reference outputs (links, version numbers); add token-diff step to rollout checklist.
- For long-thread summarization, regression tests should include at least 10 long (>1k token) threads sampled by rubric — current infra only runs medium/short by default.

Notes to self: keep this pad minimal and iterative. If we confirm scope >1% of traffic, move to a proper eval sheet with 100 samples and deterministic CI checks.

End of scratchpad.
